code:
# --- Prior over prevalence π ~ Beta(A,B) ---
# Example: a rare disease with mean prevalence ≈ 1% and moderate uncertainty.
A, B = 1.0, 99.0   # mean = A/(A+B) = 0.01

# --- Sensitivity & Specificity ---
# You can specify fixed values or Beta priors for uncertainty.
# Fixed example:
S_FIXED = 0.95     # sensitivity
C_FIXED = 0.98     # specificity

# Or, use Beta priors to reflect uncertainty (set to None to use fixed):
S_BETA = None      # e.g., (95, 5) centers ~0.95 with moderate confidence
C_BETA = None      # e.g., (98, 2) centers ~0.98 with high confidence

# Monte Carlo samples
N_SAMPLES = 100_000
print("Configured. E[π] =", A/(A+B))
description: Set Beta prior hyperparameters A = 1.0, B = 99.0 for disease prevalence, fixed sensitivity S_FIXED = 0.95 and specificity C_FIXED = 0.98, and N_SAMPLES = 100_000.

steps.description: Set the Beta prior shape parameters `A, B = 1.0, 99.0` for disease prevalence $\pi \sim \mathrm{Beta}(A, B)$.
Set fixed test sensitivity `S_FIXED = 0.95` and specificity `C_FIXED = 0.98`, and set `S_BETA = None` and `C_BETA = None` so the simulation uses the fixed values.
Set the Monte Carlo sample count `N_SAMPLES = 100_000` and print the prior mean prevalence `A / (A + B)`.
Look at lines 3 and 17: a $\mathrm{Beta}(A, B)$ distribution has expected value $E[\pi] = A / (A + B)$. Thus, `A = 1.0` and `B = 99.0` encode a prior mean prevalence of `1 / 100 = 0.01`.

steps.question: What value does `A / (A + B)` evaluate to on line 17 when `A = 1.0` and `B = 99.0`?

steps.description: Line 17 computes `A / (A + B)` and prints `Configured. E[π] = 0.01`.

title: Configuring Beta Prior Parameters, Sensitivity, Specificity, and Monte Carlo Samples
